narrative.overview: This is not a portfolio wearing a dark theme for effect. It is the literal monitoring-tool aesthetic its owner, a DevOps technical lead, builds for a living, pointed at himself: a GET /status -> 200 OK panel, route-style section labels (/checks, /about), monospace data rows, a contribution board rendered like a health graph. The site proves seniority by looking like something a senior engineer would actually leave open on a second monitor, not by claiming it in prose. The system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS landing-page vocabulary: no gradient-hero blocks, no glassmorphism, no bouncy micro-interactions, no icon set standing in for content. Status is communicated with colored dots and text arrows. Depth comes from borders and tonal surfaces, never from shadows or elevation. Two functional colors carry the entire system: Signal Cyan for information, Status Green for health. Every other value is a tinted near-black neutral.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument-panel dark theme borrowed literally from the owner's own tooling
Strict content/data split: anything that reads as output is monospace, anything that reads as prose is the display sans
No shadows, no elevation; depth is borders and surface-tone only
Two functional accents (cyan, green), each used sparingly and for one job
Fully fluid layout: clamp() and auto-fit grids, zero media-query breakpoints

rules.name: The Two-Job Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan means information/navigation. Status Green means health/availability. Neither ever borrows the other's job.

rules.name: The No-Surface-Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan and Status Green are text, borders, and small fills only. Neither is ever a background fill larger than a status dot or hover wash.

rules.name: The Output-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything that reads as a value produced by a system renders in JetBrains Mono. Anything a human wrote in full sentences renders in Space Grotesk.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to read as in front of another, give it a 1px border and a lighter background tone. Never reach for box-shadow to fake elevation.

dos: Do keep the mono/sans split total: mono for anything machine-authored, sans for anything human-authored.
Do use borders and tonal-surface steps for all depth. Nothing casts a shadow.
Do keep Signal Cyan and Status Green each doing exactly one job and nowhere else.
Do use only clamp(), auto-fit/minmax() grids, and flex-wrap for responsiveness. No media-query breakpoints anywhere.
Do make every navigation target a real <a href> with a visible 2px accent focus ring, 2px offset.
donts: Don't introduce gradient-hero blocks, glassmorphism, or bouncy micro-animations.
Don't add an icon set. Status is dots; navigation is text arrows.
Don't use box-shadow for elevation or depth; it's reserved for the two functional insets only.
Don't let Status Green appear as a link or nav color, or Signal Cyan appear as a health indicator.
Don't build identical repeating card grids as filler, or use a border-left/border-right colored stripe as an accent anywhere.
